thread.title: Special Participation A: Mistral AI's Le Chat on HW3
thread.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>Here is the online link: <link href="https://chat.mistral.ai/chat/8c72d241-dd44-41a0-b8fc-a0469d84ff1d">https://chat.mistral.ai/chat/8c72d241-dd44-41a0-b8fc-a0469d84ff1d</link></paragraph><paragraph>Here is the annotated log:</paragraph><file url="https://static.us.edusercontent.com/files/UjxEQxQUHDdCDMAgY62e9YSr" filename="Annotated log of conversation with Mistral AI.pdf"/><paragraph><bold>Executive Summary:</bold></paragraph><paragraph>From my observation, Le Chat was able to answer most written questions correctly on one shot. However, for questions that reference an external research paper, it could misunderstand the problem statement and draw something tangent to what the question is asking. In particular, it could reference a table on a different page or a formula in a different section. Doing some prompt engineering helps the model to reference the correct table/figure.</paragraph><paragraph>In addition, for questions that involve numerical counting, it could mistake the computation by a small margin, even after engineering the prompt. For instance, it could count something twice and mess up with the calculation. </paragraph></document>

Here is the online link: https://chat.mistral.ai/chat/8c72d241-dd44-41a0-b8fc-a0469d84ff1d

Here is the annotated log:

Executive Summary:

From my observation, Le Chat was able to answer most written questions correctly on one shot. However, for questions that reference an external research paper, it could misunderstand the problem statement and draw something tangent to what the question is asking. In particular, it could reference a table on a different page or a formula in a different section. Doing some prompt engineering helps the model to reference the correct table/figure.

In addition, for questions that involve numerical counting, it could mistake the computation by a small margin, even after engineering the prompt. For instance, it could count something twice and mess up with the calculation.
